identity.name: PRX Powermatic 80
identity.one_liner: The 1978 Seastar-derived integrated-bracelet design that became the default first mechanical watch of the 2020s.

provenance_events.description: Tissot reissues the 1978 PRX with a 40mm case, integrated bracelet, and Powermatic 80 movement. The 2021 reissue is the most-cited modern Tissot at its price point and one of the most-recommended entry luxury steel sports watches.

narrative.story: Tissot revived its 1978 Seastar quartz case as the PRX in 2021, first as a quartz watch and months later with the Powermatic 80 automatic and a waffle dial. It arrived exactly when steel integrated-bracelet sports watches from Patek, AP, and Vacheron had become unobtainable, and it offered the same design language for under a thousand dollars. Watch media and collectors adopted it almost immediately as the standard answer to the question of where to start.
narrative.collector_notes: The bracelet's butterfly clasp and non-quick-adjust sizing are the common gripes; the 80-hour reserve and the dial execution at this price are the reasons to forgive them. Check that the reference matches the dial variant — the PRX family shares the T137 prefix across quartz, automatic, and chronograph lines.
